root_cause: Two separate model errors keep the keeper still. (1) s7453 (Determined Acquisition counts home, so KEEPER-RELEASE returns silently at _keeper_release_primary_counts): the planner's OBJ-HOLD-2 'sole holder - leaving would drop control' treats ANY move of the keeper as a loss of the objective. It never checks where this turn's move ends. obj_home_2 is an 11e terrain-hosted objective; the keeper stands on the far edge of its hosting area. In the alternative branch (B, 2 seeds kept) the keeper's 6" Normal move toward obj_center ended at (1040,1705), still inside home's area (5.4" from the marker), and P2 still scored per_objective +3 at its R2 Command phase in both branches. So the measured gain came from holding home AND being 6" closer to the centre, not from trading home away. The 'Move' mode matters: an Advance would leave the area. (2) s7454 (P1's card does not pay for home, hold EV 0): KEEPER-RELEASE is blocked by its threat test. Log: '[KEEPER_RELEASE] obj_home_1: U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B keeps it - Custodian Guard Sodality Beta can reach it in one turn'. The enemy model is 30.7" from the marker but within M8+12+6 of the hosting area. A charge-needs-a-target reach model (Move+Advance walk-on; a 10" charge only at one of our units near the objective) released it. But it contradicts a must-pass check in test_ai_fix_keeper_release ('an M12 enemy 26" from home keeps the keeper', which encodes the max-roll model), so it was reverted and is NOT in this design.
fix_summary: FIX_KEEPER_REACH (default 1). In _assign_units_to_objectives, when the sole keeper (units_on_obj_initial<=1, not held_threatened, not released by KEEPER-RELEASE, not fragile, no HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmark) has candidates elsewhere scoring above holding (not race_lost, reachable before game end): _keeper_reach_check tries them best-first. It predicts each Normal move with the executor's own _compute_movement_toward_target (full Move, threat_data) and counts OC still in range of the held objective (_keeper_reach_oc_in_range uses MissionManager.model_in_objective_range on 11e terrain objectives, else the control circle). The first trip that keeps OC >= max(enemy_oc, projected_enemy_oc)+1 is taken after pass 2 as a Normal move. Home's OC stays counted, so no other unit is pulled onto it. DIM-RETURNS / FAR-TRIP veto it, as for KEEPER-RELEASE. The executor's Normal-move branch re-checks the actual destinations (after charge/half-range/firing-position blending); if they would leave the objective, the unit stands still. Logs are tagged [KEEPER_REACH]. 0 = base behaviour (the test checks this). KEEPER-RELEASE's threat model is unchanged.

fires: In the 8 final replays (one game each, horizon end of round 2, both players): the move fired 3 times. s7453 P2 R1 (decision), s7433 P2 R1 (decision), s7455 R2 (Prosecutors; removed by the later fragile exclusion and confirmed by a re-run). The check ran (log 'keeps OC n of m') about 15 times; most trips keep OC 0, so the keeper holds. The executor safety net ('stands still') never fired. The DIM-RETURNS veto fired once (s7451). About 0-1 fires per game.
risks: (a) The objective is chosen by planner score (best first), not by which keeping-move gains the most. At s7453 it picks nml_1 over the measured centre, and a 6-seed check showed no gain (+0.67 for hold, CI spans 0). The design can turn a hold into a neutral move without the measured benefit. (b) The keeper creeps to the edge of the objective's area, closer to the enemy. In rounds 2-5 it is easier to shoot or charge off home than a keeper in the middle. Against fast armies, the next turn's need (projected_enemy_oc) may come too late, and it ends its move with only part of its OC in range (need = enemy OC + 1, e.g. 1 model). (c) The prediction uses _compute_movement_toward_target without the executor's charge-intent, half-range or firing-position blending. The executor re-check covers the final destinations, but then the unit stands still and loses that turn's move entirely. (d) Secondary cards: none affected directly, but a unit on home's edge instead of its centre gives up nothing on cards that need home. (e) s7454 (+4.83) is not fixed; that would need KEEPER-RELEASE's max-roll threat reach replaced, which the existing keeper_release test forbids.
